extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for building, maintaining, feeding, and caring for domestic rabbits (hutch construction, cleaning, diet, young-rabbit management and simple disease treatment), aimed at beginners/young readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hutch floor construction and drainage
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the floor slope gently to the back of the hutch, and let it be double, so that the upper one can be drawn out to be cleaned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upper board should be painted with two or three coats of paint and drawn out every day to be washed and brushed. A gutter should be placed along the sloping floor to carry off drainage. After cleaning, sprinkle a layer of sand over the board when it is replaced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hutch overall dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The hutch should be from thirty to thirty-six inches long, eighteen inches wide, and about as many high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These dimensions form a recommended standard size for a single rabbit hutch intended for good care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sleeping-room partition and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Partition off the hutch by a board, leaving the sleeping-room about twelve inches long; in this board put a round hole large enough for a rabbit to pass through.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The partition improves separation of living and sleeping spaces; the access-hole should be protected by a door sliding up and down in a groove.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front construction and predator protection
rubrics_metrics.description: The simplest front is strips of wood, but galvanized (white) wire netting is preferred; mesh should not be more than three-quarters of an inch wide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire netting gives ventilation while preventing prowling cats from getting paws through. The open front should extend as far as the end of the living-room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sleeping-room door and internal shutter
rubrics_metrics.description: The sleeping-room should be inclosed by a solid door opening in the ordinary way; inside this should be a shutter about six inches high, sliding in a groove.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sliding shutter lets you open the door to look at young without danger of their falling out when the doe has babies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bedding material and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Bedding should be of straw, well broken and bruised; used only in the sleeping-room except in very cold weather.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bedding should always be dry and changed at least once a week.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hutch elevation from ground
rubrics_metrics.description: The hutch should be raised about a foot from the ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raising the hutch aids cleanliness, drainage, and protection from dampness and pests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptability of makeshift hutch shells
rubrics_metrics.description: An old packing case, if water-tight, does well enough for the shell of the hutch, but it will require some fixing up before it is ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Packing cases are a low-cost option but must be modified (floor/slope/drainage/paint) to meet the other standards described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of varied diet
rubrics_metrics.description: The principal thing in rabbit-feeding is variety, and as rabbits will eat almost every kind of vegetable, this is easily managed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying on cabbage and bran alone; provide a balanced variety of roots, grains, green food, hay, and occasional mashes as illustrated in the weekly menu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feeding frequency and portioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the sample menu provides three meals a day, rabbits are dainty and will neither eat much at a time nor return to what they have left; hence it is best to give but little at a time, and to feed regularly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller, regular portions reduce waste and suit rabbits' eating habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feeding equipment (trough design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Food should be given in a trough like a gutter, and to prevent the rabbits getting into it, it is well to fasten wires from end to end of the trough, just far enough from the sides to allow the rabbits to get their heads into it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wires prevent rabbits stepping into or soiling the feed while allowing normal access to food.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekly sample diet (menu)
rubrics_metrics.description: A suggested weekly feeding table providing varied morning, afternoon, and evening meals (examples include roots and dry oats, green food and hay, mash of potatoes and meal, soaked oats, barley, peas, bread, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table is given 'not because it need be strictly followed, but to show what is meant by variety of feeding.' Use it as an exemplar and adapt to local availability and rabbit needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doe (nursing female) feeding and management
rubrics_metrics.description: When a doe has 'babies,' she will eat nearly twice as much as at other times, and she should be separated from the little ones at her meal-times so that she may eat in peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide extra food/allowances for nursing does and ensure they have private feeding times to avoid disturbance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Young rabbit rearing and separation timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The young ones may stay with their mother for seven or eight weeks, but should then be taken away, one at a time, and put with other young rabbits; the bucks and does being kept separate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gradual separation and grouping by age/sex reduces aggression and risk; note that the father buck will often kill the little ones, so he should be kept apart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disease recognition and simple treatment (snuffles)
rubrics_metrics.description: In long wet weather or sudden cold snaps 'snuffles' may appear; symptoms are like a severe cold—running at the eyes and nose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recommended home treatment: sponge the eyes and nose with warm tea, and give a few drops of camphorated spirit twice a day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleaning schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Daily cleaning of the removable upper floor board (wash and brush) and weekly change of bedding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular daily and weekly cleaning routines are emphasized to keep the hutch 'sweet and clean' and to reduce disease risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-office Box — garden-submission content guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Little readers who have a garden which they take care of without help are invited to write what they have planted, which flowers are in bloom now, when they work in them, and what they do with their buds and blossoms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vegetable and fruit gardeners should report produce (lettuce, onions, radishes, strawberries). Young readers who earn money selling produce are invited to describe how they manage their affairs. Include concrete details of activities and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter-sender identification guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide full name rather than only initials when writing to the Post-office Box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor notes preference for full names to remember correspondents; include age and location when relevant (examples in published letters show ages and towns).
